options.name: init_config
options.description: All options defined here are available to all instances.

options.name: service
options.description:
Attach the tag `service:<SERVICE>` to every metric, event, and service check emitted by this integration.

Additionally, this sets the default `service` for every log source.

options.name: instances
options.description: Every instance is scheduled independently of the others.

options.name: panorama_host
options.description:
Hostname or IP address of a Panorama management server. When set, the Agent discovers the connected
firewalls through Panorama and polls each one directly. Set either `panorama_host` or `firewalls`, not both.
Panorama requires `panorama_username` and `panorama_password`, or `panorama_api_key`.

options.name: panorama_username
options.description: Username of a Panorama admin account with XML API Operational Requests access.

options.name: panorama_password
options.description: Password for `panorama_username`.

options.name: panorama_api_key
options.description: API key for Panorama. Use it instead of `panorama_username` and `panorama_password`.

options.name: firewall_ips
options.description:
Filters for the firewalls discovered through Panorama. Entries are IP addresses or CIDR blocks.
If no filters are configured, all connected firewalls are polled.
Use `include` to poll only matching firewalls and `exclude` to skip them. `exclude` takes precedence.

options.name: firewalls
options.description:
List of firewall IP addresses to poll. Set either `firewalls` or `panorama_host`, not both.
Every firewall must match an entry in `firewall_credentials`.

options.name: firewall_credentials
options.description:
Credentials used to log in to the firewalls. The Agent uses the first entry whose `cidr` contains the
firewall IP. An entry without `cidr` matches every firewall. Each entry must set either `username` and
`password`, or `api_key`, but not both. The same credentials apply to the firewalls found through Panorama.

options.name: namespace
options.description: Namespace to use for Network Device Monitoring (NDM) device metadata.

options.name: proxy
options.description:
This overrides the `proxy` setting in `init_config`.

Set HTTP or HTTPS proxies for this instance. Use the `no_proxy` list
to specify hosts that must bypass proxies.

The SOCKS protocol is also supported, for example:

  socks5://user:pass@host:port

Using the scheme `socks5` causes the DNS resolution to happen on the
client, rather than on the proxy server. This is in line with `curl`,
which uses the scheme to decide whether to do the DNS resolution on
the client or proxy. If you want to resolve the domains on the proxy
server, use `socks5h` as the scheme.

options.name: skip_proxy
options.description:
This overrides the `skip_proxy` setting in `init_config`.

If set to `true`, this makes the check bypass any proxy
settings enabled and attempt to reach services directly.

options.name: tls_verify
options.description:
Instructs the check to validate the TLS certificate of the firewall management interface.
PAN-OS management interfaces ship with a self-signed certificate. Either install a certificate signed
by a CA you trust and set `tls_ca_cert`, or set this to `false` to accept the self-signed certificate.

options.name: tls_use_host_header
options.description: If a `Host` header is set, this enables its use for SNI (matching against the TLS certificate CN or SAN).

options.name: tls_ignore_warning
options.description:
If `tls_verify` is disabled, security warnings are logged by the check.
Disable those by setting `tls_ignore_warning` to true.

options.name: tls_cert
options.description:
The path to a single file in PEM format containing a certificate as well as any
number of CA certificates needed to establish the certificate's authenticity for
use when connecting to services. It may also contain an unencrypted private key to use.

options.name: tls_private_key
options.description:
The unencrypted private key to use for `tls_cert` when connecting to services. This is
required if `tls_cert` is set and it does not already contain a private key.

options.name: tls_ca_cert
options.description:
The path to a file of concatenated CA certificates in PEM format, or to a directory of
PEM certificates processed with `openssl rehash`. Use it when the firewall management certificate
is signed by a private CA, or to trust a self-signed certificate directly.

options.name: tls_protocols_allowed
options.description:
The expected versions of TLS/SSL when fetching intermediate certificates.
Only `SSLv3`, `TLSv1.2`, `TLSv1.3` are allowed by default. The possible values are:
  SSLv3
  TLSv1
  TLSv1.1
  TLSv1.2
  TLSv1.3

options.name: tls_ciphers
options.description:
The list of ciphers suites to use when connecting to an endpoint. If not specified, 
`ALL` ciphers are used. For list of ciphers see: 
https://www.openssl.org/docs/man1.0.2/man1/ciphers.html

options.name: timeout
options.description: Timeout in seconds for each request to a firewall or Panorama.

options.name: connect_timeout
options.description: The connect timeout for accessing services. Defaults to `timeout`.

options.name: read_timeout
options.description: The read timeout for accessing services. Defaults to `timeout`.

options.name: request_size
options.description: The number of kibibytes (KiB) to read from streaming HTTP responses at a time.

options.name: log_requests
options.description: Whether or not to debug log the HTTP(S) requests made, including the method and URL.

options.name: persist_connections
options.description: Whether or not to persist cookies and use connection pooling for improved performance.

options.name: allow_redirects
options.description: Whether or not to allow URL redirection.

options.name: max_concurrency
options.description: Maximum number of firewalls to poll concurrently.

options.name: tags
options.description:
A list of tags to attach to every metric and service check emitted by this instance.

Learn more about tagging at https://docs.datadoghq.com/tagging

options.name: service
options.description:
Attach the tag `service:<SERVICE>` to every metric, event, and service check emitted by this integration.

Overrides any `service` defined in the `init_config` section.

options.name: min_collection_interval
options.description:
Changes the collection interval of the check. For more information, see
https://docs.datadoghq.com/developers/write_agent_check/#collection-interval.
We recommend 60 seconds. Each PAN-OS call has its own interval, from 2 minutes to 24 hours,
so a more frequent run does not collect additional data. Values above 120 seconds delay the calls
that run every 2 or 3 minutes.

options.name: empty_default_hostname
options.description:
This forces the check to send metrics with no hostname.

This is useful for cluster-level checks.

options.name: metric_patterns
options.description:
A mapping of metrics to include or exclude, with each entry being a regular expression.

Metrics defined in `exclude` will take precedence in case of overlap.

options.name: vsys
options.description:
List of virtual systems to collect from. A virtual system without interfaces is not detected
automatically, so list it here.

options.name: collect_threats
options.description: Set to `true` to count threat log entries by severity and type.

options.name: collect_rule_hits
options.description: Set to `false` to stop collecting security rule hit counts.

options.name: security_rule_filter
options.description:
List of regular expressions. Only security rules whose name matches one of them are reported.
If not set, all security rules are reported. Without a filter, one `security_rule.hits` series is sent
per security rule and virtual system, including the two default rules, which can be thousands on a
large rulebase.

options.name: collect_global_counters
options.description: Set to `true` to collect the PAN-OS global counters.

options.name: collect_ospf
options.description: Set to `true` to collect OSPF neighbor status.

options.name: collect_reports
options.description:
Set to `true` to collect the 10 top-N traffic reports (custom dynamic reports over the last 24 hours).
The reports run one at a time, and the Agent polls each one up to 10 times, 0.5 seconds apart, until it
finishes. In the worst case, where every report finishes only on its last poll, this adds about 45 seconds
of waiting, plus the time of the requests themselves, to one run every 30 minutes per firewall. A report
that is still running after its polls is picked up again by the next run.

options.name: report_top_n
options.description: Number of entries to keep from each report.

options.name: send_ndm_metadata
options.description: Set to `true` to send Network Device Monitoring metadata for the firewalls.

options.name: logs
options.description:
Log Section

type - required - Type of log input source (tcp / udp / file / windows_event).
port / path / channel_path - required - Set port if type is tcp or udp.
                                        Set path if type is file.
                                        Set channel_path if type is windows_event.
source  - required - Attribute that defines which integration sent the logs.
encoding - optional - For file specifies the file encoding. Default is utf-8. Other
                      possible values are utf-16-le and utf-16-be.
service - optional - The name of the service that generates the log.
                     Overrides any `service` defined in the `init_config` section.
tags - optional - Add tags to the collected logs.

Discover Datadog log collection: https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/log_collection/
